issues.description: Inline negated predicate buries intent; extract a named helper like isLayerStatement(node).
issues.detail: `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` reads as a puzzle and hides the real contract: a block-less @layer statement is allowed before @import, a @layer with a block is not. A named helper such as `isLayerStatement(node)` or `hasLayerBlock(node)` would make the invariant self-evident at the call site.

issues.description: Use `node.nodes == null` instead of `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` to match codebase idioms.
issues.detail: The `typeof === 'undefined'` form is defensive verbiage for a value PostCSS controls and doesn't match the surrounding style. `node.nodes == null` is shorter, conventional here, and directly reflects PostCSS's container-vs-leaf data shape without leaking the internal field check across abstraction boundaries.

issues.description: Add an accept-case test pinning `@layer foo;` (statement form) as still valid before `@import`.
issues.detail: The new test covers the bug (layer-with-block rejected), but no test asserts the still-allowed statement form `@layer foo;` before `@import`. Without a paired accept case, a future refactor of the predicate could silently regress the originally allowed behavior. One extra fixture locks the data distinction both ways.

synthesis.summary: Small, scoped, correct patch that restores the CSS spec distinction between `@layer foo;` (statement, allowed before `@import`) and `@layer foo {}` (block, not allowed). All three reviewers agree the behavior is right and the change is appropriately sized. The only concerns are expression-level: the inline negated predicate buries intent and would read better as a named helper, the `typeof === 'undefined'` check should match codebase idioms via `== null`, and the test suite should pin the still-allowed statement form alongside the new reject case. Verdict: ACCEPT after trivial fixup.
